$$s(t) = 2t^3 - 5t^2 + 3t$$

The displacement at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is $2\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Acceleration model calibrated by dual displacement conditions with turning point analysis

hints: Integrate acceleration twice: $v(t) = 3t^2 - 18t + p$, then $s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2 + pt + q$.
Substitute $t = 1, s = 21$: $1 - 9 + p + q = 21 \implies p + q = 29$.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate the acceleration function twice with constants of integration $p$ and $q$:
$$v(t) = \int (6t - 18)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3t^2 - 18t + p$$
$$s(t) = \int (3t^2 - 18t + p)\,\mathrm{d}t = t^3 - 9t^2 + pt + q$$

Substitute the two given boundary conditions into the displacement equation:
$$s(1) = (1)^3 - 9(1)^2 + p(1) + q = 21 \implies p + q - 8 = 21 \implies p + q = 29$$
$$s(3) = (3)^3 - 9(3)^2 + p(3) + q = 23 \implies 27 - 81 + 3p + q = 23 \implies 3p + q = 77$$

Solve the system of linear equations:
$$(3p + q) - (p + q) = 77 - 29 \implies 2p = 48 \implies p = 24$$
$$q = 29 - 24 = 5$$
$$s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2 + 24t + 5$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Perform two-stage integration:
- General displacement:
$$s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2 + pt + q$$

Construct simultaneous system:
- Equations at $t = 1$ and $t = 3$:
$$p + q = 29, \quad 3p + q = 77$$

Solve for parameters:
- Linear elimination:
$$p = 24, \quad q = 5$$
The constants are $p = 24$ and $q = 5$.

ai_rubric.observable: Integrates acceleration twice: $v = 3t^2 - 18t + p$ and $s = t^3 - 9t^2 + pt + q$.
Sets up simultaneous equations: $p + q - 8 = 21 \implies p + q = 29$ and $3p + q - 54 = 23 \implies 3p + q = 77$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone 1: Fractional acceleration model with stationary velocity extrema and multi-point displacement evaluation

hints: Stationary points of velocity occur when $a = 0$: $3(t - 4\sqrt{t} + 3) = 0 \implies (\sqrt{t} - 1)(\sqrt{t} - 3) = 0$.

The roots are $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 9\text{ s}$. Test $\frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{d}t} = 3 - 6t^{-1/2}$; at $t = 9$, $\frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{d}t} = 3 - 2 = 1 > 0$, so $t = 9\text{ s}$ is the minimum.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate the acceleration function term by term with $v(0) = 0$:
$$v(t) = \int \left(3t - 12t^{1/2} + 9\right)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) - 12\left(\frac{2}{3}t^{3/2}\right) + 9t + C$$
$$v(0) = 0 \implies C = 0 \implies v(t) = \frac{3}{2}t^2 - 8t^{3/2} + 9t$$

Integrate the velocity function to obtain the displacement function with $s(0) = 0$:
$$s(t) = \int \left(\frac{3}{2}t^2 - 8t^{3/2} + 9t\right)\,\mathrm{d}t = \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{t^3}{3}\right) - 8\left(\frac{2}{5}t^{5/2}\right) + 9\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) + D$$
$$s(t) = \frac{1}{2}t^3 - \frac{16}{5}t^{5/2} + \frac{9}{2}t^2$$
$$s(0) = 0 \implies D = 0$$

Locate stationary points of velocity by setting acceleration to zero:
$$3t - 12t^{1/2} + 9 = 0$$
$$3(t - 4t^{1/2} + 3) = 0$$
$$3(t^{1/2} - 1)(t^{1/2} - 3) = 0 \implies t^{1/2} = 1 \implies t = 1\text{ s}, \quad \text{or } t^{1/2} = 3 \implies t = 9\text{ s}$$

Verify the minimum velocity using the second derivative and evaluate at $t = 9\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{d}t} = 3 - 6t^{-1/2} \implies \text{at } t = 9, \quad 3 - \frac{6}{3} = 1 > 0 \quad (\text{minimum})$$
$$v(9) = \frac{3}{2}(9)^2 - 8(9)^{3/2} + 9(9) = \frac{3}{2}(81) - 8(27) + 81 = 121.5 - 216 + 81 = -13.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Antidifferentiate acceleration:
- Velocity and displacement functions:
$$v(t) = \frac{3}{2}t^2 - 8t^{3/2} + 9t, \quad s(t) = \frac{1}{2}t^3 - \frac{16}{5}t^{5/2} + \frac{9}{2}t^2$$

Find stationary points:
- Quadratic in $\sqrt{t}$:
$$(\sqrt{t} - 1)(\sqrt{t} - 3) = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}, \quad t = 9\text{ s}$$

Identify minimum:
- Second derivative is positive at $t = 9\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{d}t}\Big|_{t=9} = 1 > 0$$

Evaluate minimum velocity:
- Substitution:
$$v(9) = 121.5 - 216 + 81 = -13.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The minimum velocity is $-13.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets acceleration to zero: $3(t - 4t^{1/2} + 3) = 3(t^{1/2} - 1)(t^{1/2} - 3) = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}, t = 9\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the displacement formula at $t = 9\text{ s}$ using exact powers of 9:
$$s(9) = \frac{1}{2}(9)^3 - \frac{16}{5}(9)^{5/2} + \frac{9}{2}(9)^2$$
$$s(9) = \frac{729}{2} - \frac{16}{5}(243) + \frac{729}{2} = 729 - \frac{3888}{5} = 729 - 777.6 = -48.6\text{ m}$$

Evaluate the displacement formula at $t = 4\text{ s}$ using exact powers of 4:
$$s(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)^3 - \frac{16}{5}(4)^{5/2} + \frac{9}{2}(4)^2$$
$$s(4) = \frac{64}{2} - \frac{16}{5}(32) + \frac{9}{2}(16) = 32 - 102.4 + 72 = 104 - 102.4 = 1.6\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate position at minimum velocity ($t = 9\text{ s}$):
- Arithmetic:
$$s(9) = 729 - 777.6 = -48.6\text{ m}$$

Evaluate position at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
- Arithmetic:
$$s(4) = 104 - 102.4 = 1.6\text{ m}$$
The displacements are $-48.6\text{ m}$ at $t = 9\text{ s}$ and $1.6\text{ m}$ at $t = 4\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone 2: Staggered multi-particle motion reconstruction with boundary calibration and spatial separation

hints: For particle $Q$: $v_Q(t) = \int (6t - 12)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3t^2 - 12t + C$. Starts from rest at $t = 2 \implies 3(4) - 24 + C = 0 \implies C = 12$.
Integrate $v_Q$: $s_Q(t) = \int 3(t - 2)^2\,\mathrm{d}t = (t - 2)^3 + D$. Starts at $O$ at $t = 2 \implies D = 0$, so $s_Q(t) = (t - 2)^3$.

walkthrough.text:
Derive velocity and displacement expressions for particle $P$:
$$v_P(t) = \int (6 - 2t)\,\mathrm{d}t = 6t - t^2 + C_P \implies v_P(0) = 5 \implies v_P(t) = 6t - t^2 + 5$$
$$s_P(t) = \int (6t - t^2 + 5)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3t^2 - \frac{1}{3}t^3 + 5t + D_P \implies s_P(0) = 0 \implies s_P(t) = 3t^2 - \frac{1}{3}t^3 + 5t$$

Derive velocity for particle $Q$ using the boundary condition $v_Q(2) = 0$:
$$v_Q(t) = \int (6t - 12)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3t^2 - 12t + C_Q$$
$$v_Q(2) = 3(2)^2 - 12(2) + C_Q = 12 - 24 + C_Q = 0 \implies C_Q = 12$$
$$v_Q(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 12 = 3(t - 2)^2$$

Derive displacement for particle $Q$ using the boundary condition $s_Q(2) = 0$:
$$s_Q(t) = \int 3(t - 2)^2\,\mathrm{d}t = (t - 2)^3 + D_Q$$
$$s_Q(2) = 0 \implies D_Q = 0 \implies s_Q(t) = (t - 2)^3$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Reconstruct particle $P$ motion:
- Initial conditions at $t = 0$:
$$v_P(t) = 6t - t^2 + 5, \quad s_P(t) = 3t^2 - \frac{1}{3}t^3 + 5t$$

Reconstruct particle $Q$ motion:
- Staggered conditions at $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$v_Q(t) = 3(t - 2)^2, \quad s_Q(t) = (t - 2)^3$$
The derived functions are confirmed for $t \ge 2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone 2: Staggered multi-particle motion reconstruction with boundary calibration and spatial separation

hints: Distance between particles is $|s_P(4) - s_Q(4)| = \frac{140}{3} - 8 = \frac{116}{3}\text{ m} \approx 38.7\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the velocity of both particles at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$v_P(4) = 6(4) - (4)^2 + 5 = 24 - 16 + 5 = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v_Q(4) = 3(4 - 2)^2 = 3(2)^2 = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Evaluate the displacement of both particles from $O$ at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$s_P(4) = 3(4)^2 - \frac{1}{3}(4)^3 + 5(4) = 48 - \frac{64}{3} + 20 = 68 - \frac{64}{3} = \frac{140}{3}\text{ m}$$
$$s_Q(4) = (4 - 2)^3 = (2)^3 = 8\text{ m}$$

Compute the distance between the two particles:
$$\text{Separation} = s_P(4) - s_Q(4) = \frac{140}{3} - 8 = \frac{140 - 24}{3} = \frac{116}{3}\text{ m} \approx 38.7\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate velocities at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
- Direct evaluations:
$$v_P(4) = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v_Q(4) = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Evaluate positions at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
- Values from $O$:
$$s_P(4) = \frac{140}{3}\text{ m}, \quad s_Q(4) = 8\text{ m}$$

Calculate separation distance:
- Subtraction:
$$\frac{140}{3} - 8 = \frac{116}{3}\text{ m} \approx 38.7\text{ m}$$
At $t = 4\text{ s}$, the velocities are $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$, separated by $\frac{116}{3}\text{ m}$.
